newsitem.title: USA: Best sued over $2.74 million in products.
newsitem.headline: Best sued over $2.74 million in products.

text.p: Sharp Electronics Corp, the U.S. sales arm of Japan's Sharp Corp, filed a lawsuit in federal court Wednesday seeking to reclaim about $2.74 million worth of electronics products that it had shipped to retailer Best Products Co Inc.
Sharp shipped the products to Best on credit but has yet to be paid, according to the lawsuit.

Best announced Monday that it had stopped making payments to its suppliers and was not receiving merchandise shipments as it pondered its options, including filing for bankruptcy court protection again. The company filed for Chapter 11 protection in January 1991 and emerged in June 1994.

In the lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in Richmond, Sharp sought a temporary restraining order to stop Best from selling any of the products that it shipped for ten days, preserving Sharp's right to reclaim them.
A hearing on the request was scheduled for Friday.
Best spokesman Ross Richardson said the company had no comment because it does not discuss pending litigation.
